notes:
## Improvements

- **New Suivelle logo:** A rounded frame left open at the top right with a dot stepping into the gap, for space made for the work that matters. It replaces the S and star in the title bar, app icon, taskbar, installer, favicon and the website.
- **Spreadsheet-style table editing:** Pick a block of cells with `Shift+arrows`, `Shift+click` or a drag (`Ctrl+A` picks every loaded cell, and pressed again ticks every row); `Ctrl+C` copies it as tab-separated text and a table, and `Ctrl+V` pastes text or a copied range, matching each column's type (options by name, multi-select by comma list, relations by record title) and adding new records when the paste runs past the last row. Cells in calculated columns or with no matching option are skipped and counted in a message. `Ctrl+D` and `Ctrl+R` fill down and right, the handle at the corner of the block fills by dragging and keeps counting numbers and days, and `Delete` clears the whole block. `Ctrl+Z` and `Ctrl+Y` undo and redo cell edits (a paste or fill is one step; cells changed since are skipped). `Enter` on the last row starts a new record, typing in a select or status cell opens its list with what you typed, and double-clicking a column edge fits it to its content.
- **Excel-style formulas:** New functions for logic (`and`, `or`, `not`, `switch`, `iferror`, `coalesce`), maths (`mod`, `pow`, `sqrt`, `ln`, `log10`, `sign`, `sum`, `average`, `median`), text (`lower`, `upper`, `trim`, `replace`, `replaceAll`, `left`, `right`, `mid`, `split`, `join`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `padStart`), dates (`year`, `month`, `day`, `weekday`, `week`, `dateBetween`, `startOf`, `endOf`) and lists (`first`, `last`, `at`, `unique`, `sort`). The formula editor suggests function and property names as you type (`Enter` or `Tab` to accept), shows the arguments of the function under the cursor, and marks the exact spot of a mistake, which you can click to select. Existing formulas keep working.
- **Column totals & group summaries:** A totals row at the bottom of the table sums up each column over every matching record, not just the rows loaded: click a footer cell to choose Count, Empty, Filled, % filled, Sum, Average, Median, Min, Max, Range, Earliest, Latest, Date range or % checked, whichever fits the column. Group headers show the same summaries for their group, and selecting a block of cells shows a small strip with its count, sum and average.
- **Number display formatting:** Number, rollup and number-formula properties can have a display format: decimals, a thousands separator, percent, a currency symbol, a unit suffix, and an optional progress bar behind the number. Only the display changes; copying and editing still use the plain value.
- **Conditional formatting:** A new **Format** button in table views colours rows or single cells when a condition holds, using the same conditions as filters, so overdue dates, low stock or finished tasks stand out. Rules are saved with the view and the first matching rule wins.
- **Database view search:** Press `Ctrl+F` in a table (or use the **Search** button in the toolbar) and type to show only records with that text in a title, text, link, email, phone or option name, with the matches highlighted. The search works on top of the view's filter and sort, so the count and totals follow it, and it works in list, board, gallery and the other record views too.
- **Find & replace and deduplication:** A new `…` menu in table views has **Find and replace** (one property or every text property in the view, with Match case and Whole cell options, a count of what will change before anything does, and one Undo) and **Remove duplicates** (pick the properties that must match, preview the groups, and move the extra records to the trash, keeping the oldest, with Undo).
- **Data checks & default values:** Properties can have data checks and a default value: required, unique, a smallest and largest value or length, and an email or web address format on text. Cells that break a check get a red corner and a note on hover, but nothing is blocked, so pasting and importing keep working. A default value fills new records.
- **Faster cell & column menus:** Right-click a cell and choose **Filter by this value** or **Exclude this value** to add it to the view's filter. Column header menus gain **Filter**, **Group by this property**, **Insert left** and **Insert right**, **Duplicate property** (with its values), **Wrap text** and **Freeze columns up to here**.
- **Row height & frozen columns:** Table views have a row height (**Compact**, **Medium** or **Tall**) and can keep up to three columns beside the title in place while you scroll sideways, both set from the `…` menu. Wrapped columns show several lines in Tall rows.
- **Ten new database templates:** **New from template** adds Reading List, Contacts & Deals, Content Calendar, Expense Tracker, Job Search, Inventory, Recipe Book, Meeting Notes, Habit Tracker, and Goals & OKRs (objectives with key results whose progress rolls up). Each comes with sample records, suitable property types, and views such as a board, calendar, gallery or chart, plus totals rows and calculated columns where they help. They are ordinary databases you can rename and extend.
- **Overview pages for starters:** The page that holds a starter's databases (Software Project, Reading List and the rest) starts with a short description, a link to each database with a line about what it holds, and live views of the most useful ones, such as the current sprint board, open bugs, the pipeline or a calendar, so you land on something useful instead of an empty page. It is ordinary page content you can edit or delete.
- **Pivot view:** A new **Pivot** view turns a database into a cross-table: pick a property for the rows and another for the columns (select, status, checkbox or date, with day, week, month or year for dates), then choose Count, Sum, Average, Min or Max of a number. Totals for every row and column and a grand total are included, calculated over all matching records, and numbers use the property’s display format. The view honours its filter and the shared dashboard filters.
- **Export view as CSV:** Any database view can be saved as a spreadsheet file: right-click its tab and choose **Export view as CSV**. The file keeps the view’s filter and sort, its visible columns in their order, and readable values such as option names. Text that could run as a formula in a spreadsheet is made safe.
- **Paste a table on import:** Import has a new **Paste a table** button: copy cells from Excel or Google Sheets, paste them in, and get the same preview as a file, with the first row as column names and the column types guessed (you can change them first). Commas, quotes and line breaks inside cells come through intact, and `.tsv` files now always split on tabs.
- **Live-synced database views:** Every view of a database stays current: edit a record, a property or a view in one pane and charts, pivots, totals, boards, calendars, galleries and tables showing the same data (in other panes, embedded in pages or on dashboards) update within a moment, without reloading.
- **Multi-row actions & record undo:** `Ctrl+Z` in a table moves a record you just made (or duplicated) to the trash, and `Ctrl+Y` brings it back. Right-clicking a row that is part of a selection, whether ticked rows or a block of cells, now acts on all of them: **Move to trash**, **Duplicate** or **Open** apply to every selected record, with Undo. "New record" no longer shows the new row twice.
- **Drag-to-scroll boards & views:** Hold the left mouse button on empty space in a board and drag to move it sideways or up and down, with easing and a little momentum (cards still drag as before). The middle button does the same in tables, boards, galleries, calendars and timelines.
- **Middle-button hand scrolling on pages:** In a page, the middle mouse button is now a hand, as on the canvas: hold it anywhere and drag to scroll with easing and momentum, and the browser’s circular auto-scroll never appears. The left button still selects text and edits as usual.
- **Split-pane drag & drop:** Dragging a split pane by its header lifts it out of the layout so the other panes reflow, shows a chip with its title under the pointer, and previews exactly where it will land on every edge or as a swap; letting go elsewhere or pressing `Escape` puts it back. The drop preview also no longer slides in from the top-left corner.
- **Consistent block-handle gutter:** Pages everywhere (main view, split panes, the peek panel and narrow windows) keep room on the left for the block handle, so the add and drag buttons no longer stick out of the page.
- **Minimum split-pane size:** Split panes can no longer be dragged narrower than `360 px` or shorter than `280 px`, so a pane never shrinks to an unreadable sliver.
- **Organised Settings layout:** Settings pages are organised into titled sections with a one-line description and a card of rows: **Layout and motion** (Shape and lines, Window frame, Icons, Size and spacing, Motion), **Editor** (with the sample on top), **Window and startup** (Startup, Tray), **Data and backups** (Backups, Files, Storage health), **Appearance** (Mode, Accent) and **About**. Each page opens with a short note on what it is for.
- **Drag-to-scroll in Settings:** Hold the mouse on empty space in Settings and drag, and the page follows with easing and a little momentum. Buttons, switches, fields and text you can select still behave as usual.
- **Octopolis Updates page & changelogs:** The Updates page is restyled like Octopolis: a status card with a tone tile, tidier automatic-update rows, and a **What’s new** section for your version with a **View changelogs** button that opens every release, folded by version. Changelog views now render full Markdown with clean, non-selectable typography.
- **Steady tooltips:** Tooltips no longer jump between one line and several while they grow or move between buttons; the text keeps its final shape and is revealed as the bubble resizes.
- **Tidier Shortcuts and input:** Context chips replace the dropdowns, each context is its own card with its key caps on the right, edited shortcuts are tagged, and **Disable**, **Add** and **Reset** appear when you hover a row.
- **Command palette shortcut:** The command palette now opens with `Ctrl+P` (`Ctrl+K` no longer opens it). You can still rebind it in **Settings > Shortcuts and input**.
- **Disabled browser shortcuts:** The browser shortcuts built into the window (print, save page, view source, reload, find next, caret browsing and zoom keys) are switched off, so none of them can pop up over the app.
- **Fuzzy palette search:** The palette matches fuzzily (`"swtch"` finds "Switch to dark theme") and puts what you use most first, for commands and pages.
- **Icon customisation:** **Layout and motion** adds Icon style (Outlined, Rounded, Sharp), Icon weight and Icon fill.
- **Drag-over tab opening:** Holding a dragged page over a tab for a moment fills the tab with a bar and opens it. A closed split pane shrinks and fades away.
- **Octopolis split panes & tabs:** Dragging a tab, page or pane over a pane now works like Octopolis: every edge pulses, the edge under the pointer glows and a skeleton of the new pane shows where it will open. Split panes are separate rounded cards, the focused one outlined, and new panes grow in. Tabs use the same darker strip with a lit top edge on the current tab.
- **Tabbed Agents settings:** **Settings > Agents** is split into five tabs (General, Agents, Usage, Memory, Files) instead of one long page, with a count of waiting proposals on General.
- **Material Symbols icons:** Every interface icon is now a Google Material Symbol, the same set Octopolis uses.
- **Octopolis app chrome:** The whole app now uses the Octopolis look: the page, toolbar and tabs sit on one raised card over the window frame, buttons and menus use stronger outlines, and corners are slightly tighter.
- **17 curated themes:** **Appearance** offers 17 themes grouped as Light, Dark, High contrast, Minimal, Vibrant and Pastel, each shown as a small preview. Text and status colours in every theme are adjusted just enough to stay readable. The default is now **Octopolis Midnight** (dark) and **Paper** (light).
- **Cleaner Recent list:** The sidebar's Recent list no longer repeats pages that are already in Favorites.
- **Larger sidebar toggle:** The sidebar collapse button has a larger click area.
- **Board scroll fade:** Board views fade the edge where more columns are waiting to be scrolled into view.
- **Streamlined Appearance settings:** In Settings, **Appearance** keeps the palette presets and preview up front and tucks the individual colour rows under **Fine-tune individual colors**.
- **Compact sidebar footer:** The sidebar's Trash, Backups, Import & export and Settings buttons now sit in one compact row of icons. Hover any of them to see its name.
- **Shared Node Map & Inbox row:** Node Map and the agents Inbox now share one row at the top of the sidebar, and Node Map fills the row when there is no Inbox.
- **Uncropped page icons:** Page icons in the sidebar and elsewhere are no longer cropped: images that aren't square are shown whole, and emoji are no longer clipped.
- **Smooth toggle switches:** Toggle switches settle smoothly instead of overshooting.
- **Customisable titlebar controls:** **Settings > Layout and motion** now lets you switch between Windows titlebar buttons and macOS traffic lights (placed on the left or right), and the titlebar blends cleanly with the window background.
- **Smoother canvas boards:** The board title pill hugs its title over a frosted surface, cards animate in with subtle elevation and optional accent tinting, page cards can fold to their header or zoom to fit on a double-click, middle-clicking pans from anywhere (including inside embedded pages), minimap clicks glide smoothly, connector handles and edges highlight their targets and stay easy to grab when zoomed out, and the dot grid tracks your pan and zoom.
- **Native Win32 tray menu:** Right-clicking the tray icon now opens a lightweight native menu instantly without using extra background memory, synced live with your theme, accent colour, spacing, corner style and display scaling, and positioned next to the icon away from the taskbar. `Escape`, arrow keys or clicking elsewhere navigate and dismiss it.
